**Group:** Detritus  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A non-living detrital particle from zooplankton grazing, in the elongated form: a long, cylindrical to rod- or sausage-shaped compact mass with a defined outline, often darker and more uniform than a loose aggregate and sometimes enclosed by a thin membrane. Length is markedly greater than width. Key features: elongate cylindrical/rod shape, defined outline, compact contents.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **fecal_pellet_short** | The short form is stubby or ovoid with length close to width; the long form is distinctly elongated and rod-like. |
| **aggregate** | Aggregates are loose, irregular flocs with diffuse edges; fecal pellets are compact particles with a defined outline. |
